title: Looking for advice on creating character assets for a fighting game
author: scumbag-deluxe
selftext:
I need some assets for a fighting game I’m working on, specifically playable 3D characters.

My idea was to take a 3D image/model of a fighter, for example a karateka or street fighter, and use something like Meshy to turn it into a textured 3D model. My first attempt actually looked pretty good as a static model, although it ended up being quite heavy at around 600k polygons. I assume that could be reduced quite a bit with some optimization/retopology.

The next challenge is the fighting animations. I assume I would need to rig the Meshy character with a skeleton first. Is it possible to then use generic fighting-game animations (punch, kick, roundhouse kick, etc.) and retarget those animations to the character's rig in Blender or a similar tool? Ideally, I’d like to use existing animation/mocap libraries rather than having to create all the animations myself.

Are there better workflows for creating something like this? Would it make more sense to subscribe to one of the online services that generate game-ready characters/assets? Meshy and Tripo, for example, aren’t particularly expensive.

In the end I’ll probably need around 10–15 different characters/assets, so I’m trying to figure out what would be the most practical workflow before committing to anything. 

Any tips or recommendations would be greatly appreciated!

comments.author: Opening_Wafer_6584
comments.body:
Hey! Alex here from the Tripo Studio US team.

Yes, the general workflow you’re describing is possible. The main thing is separating character generation from animation readiness.

A generated character can look good as a static model, but for a fighting game the harder part is usually getting it into a state where it rigs, deforms, and retargets well. In practice, a pretty normal workflow would be:

* generate the base character
* clean up / reduce topology
* rig the character
* retarget existing animations or mocap
* test deformation in-engine

So yes, you can absolutely use existing punch / kick / roundhouse type animations instead of creating everything from scratch. I’d just strongly recommend testing one representative fighter through the full pipeline before committing to 10–15 characters, because the animation/cleanup side is usually where the real time cost shows up.

If your goal is realism, I’d expect the biggest challenge to be less “can I get a fighter model” and more “can I get consistent, believable animation and deformation across the roster.”
